minAgeNotes._all: JUDGEMENT, NOT A CITATION. Source 11 (Narvekar) put its patient-reported instrument at >=8, but that floor attaches to a 0-10 numeric rating scale over a 24h recall window, its pediatric evidence is four children aged 9-10, and importing it would silence EVERY question here for the 4-7 tier -- a tier the app already serves with two unevidenced hand-written questions. The honest form: the 4-7 wording of items 1, 2, 3 and 10 is the least supported thing in the repo.

judgement.itemRank: Proposed, not yet confirmed by review.
judgement.rankingPrinciple: Decision 9: no item is ranked highly because a model names it. The two model variables (items 8, 9) rank eighth and ninth, below eight guideline-only items.
judgement.item1Exception: Decision 3: item 1 may use a CATEGORY cue (the general kind of substance), a deliberate narrow exception to the never-name-the-chemical ban. Naming a specific chemical stays banned.
judgement.item10: The single most consequential item in the packet and the worst-sourced -- one guideline, one clause. Kept because it is the only child-reportable discriminator for orbital involvement.
judgement.item11: Demoted, not deleted. If a two-option answer widget ever ships, item 11 is the first to promote and should REPLACE item 8, not join it.
judgement.unenforceableCautions: Decision 3's bound on the item-1 exception -- 'a generator must not read this decision as permission to list hazards' -- is prose only. Nothing distinguishes a permitted category cue from an enumerated hazard list, so item 1's candidates need a human eye at review rather than a screen rule.
